title: French and Bulgarian presidents condemn violence at Marseille v Levski Europa League game
summary: Emmanuel Macron: incidents had ‘no place in sport’ Nazi salutes alleged among Levski Sofia fans The presidents of France and Bulgaria have condemned violence that broke out at a Europa League fixture between Marseille and Levski Sofia in the Stade Vélodrome. Television footage showed Marseille fans cornering a group of Levski supporters in the stands before beating them relentlessly, including with a belt. One Levski fan is seen bleeding from the head as he receives multiple blows while trying to protect a female friend. Reports from inside the stadium on Thursday suggested violence began after a Levski supporter was seen making a Nazi salute. Continue reading...

title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
summary: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer. On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. title: Bills, Eagles and Bears pull off last-gasp wins in trio of Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Bass hits from 57 yards at the gun to lift Buffalo Elliott’s 59-yarder caps Eagles’ 21-point comeback Bears take NFC North lead on Odunze’s late catch After sharing top billing, Buffalo’s Josh Allen and Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes proved no match for the elements in the latest showdown of two of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. With both offense’s failing to gain traction on a rainy, windy and cold Thursday night, the Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1 by slogging through a 13-10 victory over the visiting Chiefs on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. Buffalo have won seven straight and matched their best start to a season since 1991. Continue reading...

title: All Blacks have ‘no gas in the tank’ but stats show it’s England who should be out of juice
summary: Figures indicate England’s players have far more rugby miles in their legs than Saturday’s opponents but Borthwick has managed to balance heavy schedule The prevailing narrative emerging before England’s rematch with New Zealand on Saturday is that the All Blacks are running on fumes. The forwards coach, Jason Ryan, has said that “there is not much juice in the tank” while Graham Henry, who led them to the 2011 World Cup title, has continued the theme in even starker terms. “It’s the end of the season and we’re buggered. They’ve just got no gas in the tank.” It is understood that narrative has raised a number of eyebrows within the England camp. The view, as England seek to clinch a third straight win over New Zealand for the first time in the history of the fixture, is best summed up as, “welcome to our world”. We are nearing the end of a gruelling year for the All Blacks, who give the impression they cannot wait for their season to end, but the grind in England, that which led to Maro Itoje being ordered to take the summer off, is at the very least comparable. Continue reading...

title: No sanctions and no recrimination: Cricket Australia ball tampering forum to include 2017-18 Ashes series
summary: Scope of forum includes Australia’s entire 2017-18 season Independent process to be led by senior counsel Fiona McLeod The scope of a forum set up to provide Australian players and staff on the 2018 tour of South Africa with an opportunity to air their views on sandpapergate has been broadened to include experiences from the 2017-18 Ashes series. title: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished. But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

title: Mike Tomlin calls Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ as Brady rips Rodgers for breaking locker room sanctity
summary: Ex-coach says QB was ‘beloved’ by teammates Rodgers released after diatribe about McCarthy Mike Tomlin, who coached Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers last year, and Tom Brady, one of Rodgers’s longtime peers as an elite quarterback, ⁠weighed in Thursday on the 42-year-old’s dramatic exit from Pittsburgh this week. “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin said at half-time of NBC’s Thanksgiving night broadcast of the Kansas City Chiefs-Buffalo Bills game. “It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.” Continue reading...

title: Overton’s fiery five-wicket haul helps England to flip Gabba script against Australia
summary: No ground in Australia is more associated with ritual guttings of English cricket teams than the so-called Gabbatoir. They usually leave in a state of disarray, beaten up on the field and with ears still ringing from abuse on the boundary’s edge. Yet on a muggy Friday night on Vulture Street, the locals had precious little material to work with and the traditional script had been flipped on its head. Driven by Jamie Overton’s fiery five-wicket haul, England wiped the floor with their hosts for the second match in a row to claim a 2-1 lead with two to play. Continue reading...
